Then action produce gives 2 goods, sell at price... Selling next rounds with devaluation. Buy 3 units at 12+10+9=31, cash 6.65. Then can sell later? Prices: selling 3 units back moves counter. Actually selling gives 12+10+9=31 back minus nothing, but devaluation rounds 5-6: cash floor/100*62. Buying goods lets sell later at same prices only if counter reset—but counter would have moved back. Currently counter 0, so buying now just reverses own future sales. Better: don't buy; produce 2 goods and sell them. Buy just converts cash to goods at same price — cash loses ~38% devaluation each round, so holding goods is better? Selling later: sell 2 units get 12+10=22 alashi fresh cash. Buying 2 now costs 22, then sell later get 22 — avoids devaluation loss of cash. Yes! Holding cash loses 38% per round. Buy 2 units for 22, then cash 18.65, sell later 22 back. Buy 3 costs 31, later sell 3 for 31, cash left 6.65→devalued but small. But rivals also sell, pushing counter up, lowering prices. Risky. Buying 2 seems safe-ish? Counter at 0, others hold goods 2 (idx0) who may sell. If others sell first, prices drop. Devaluation is 38% per round, two rounds to end (rounds 5,6 markets). Buying 2 saves ~22*0.62^2 ≈ 8.5 loss. Also produce 2 more goods → 4 goods to sell later, price falls anyway. Actually my future sales push counter up regardless.

Buy 2: convert 22 cash to goods, sell in round 5/6 at 12,10. Cash 18.65→ deval to ~11.5, ~7.2... total similar. Alternatively buy 3 (31) keeps only 6.65 cash, but then selling 3 later gets 31, saving 31*0.62^2≈12 lost. But selling 3 lowers price for remaining own goods. With produce+shuttle I'll have more goods than sale slots... In rounds 5-6 I can sell up to? Each market one sell action; can sell many units. Total own goods ~3(bought)+2(produce)+shuttle... plenty; prices drop to 1 anyway after several units. Marginal price beyond ~5 units low. So buy3: my first 3 sales return 31 regardless — same total revenue as more goods. Buying avoids devaluation on 31 alashi. Choose buy 3.
